item.title: National grant helps preserve two historic Black churches in Indiana
item.description: Two churches in Indiana have been selected to be part of the National Trust for Historic Preservation’s Preserving Black Churches grant program.

item.title: Data center proposed for Decatur Township wins first step toward approval
item.description: Despite visible community opposition, a proposed 130-acre data center in Decatur Township cleared a key hurdle Thursday, moving one step closer to approval.

item.title: Student volunteers at west side school send 20,000 meals to Haiti
item.description: Indianapolis students at a west side school volunteered Thursday to help send 20,000 meals to kids in Haiti.

item.title: Authors of 'banned books' speak at Indianapolis schools
item.description: During the 2024-2025 school year, 6,870 books were challenged or banned in public school districts, according to PEN America. That's more than twice as many bans as two years ago.

item.title: Missing child alert updates inspired by Hailey Buzbee's death approved by statehouse
item.description: Lawmakers gave final approval for a bill that slightly changes the state’s alert system for missing or endangered children in the wake of the disappearance and death of 17-year-old Hailey Buzbee.

item.title: Advocates say lawmakers have pushed legislation making it harder to be homeless, struggle with substance abuse in Indiana
item.description: Advocates gathered at the statehouse to pushback on a bill that would criminalize homelessness. They say lawmakers are writing legislation that impacts them without a seat at the table.

item.title: IPS Superintendent Aleesia Johnson: Families must stay engaged as the city shifts to mayor-appointed education board
item.description: IPS Superintendent Aleesia Johnson says her top priority is maintaining stability for families as a new mayor-appointed board will take over large pieces of the city’s divided education system.

item.title: Your electric bill is going to change. New law aims to stabilize utilities
item.description: The measure is one of lawmakers’ efforts to address pocketbook issues this year as demand for energy and electric bills rise.

item.title: Indiana cracks down on kids' social media, cell phones in school
item.description: Indiana lawmakers have approved sweeping new restrictions on children’s access to social media and cell phones.

item.title: 2026 session wrap: Did Indiana lawmakers deliver on affordability?
item.description: Indiana lawmakers concluded the 2026 legislative session Friday. Deregulatory bills and legislation to entice the Chicago Bears to move across state lines passed. Democrats say efforts to improve affordability fell short.
